column8: Mon 16 Nov: Keel's method (voice rounds, aha cold tests, exhibit reads): write each check's target before the round and report the interval beside the count; serves no report part directly, so F 3.
Mon 16 Nov: method only; the bars are conventions (ERIC calls them arbitrary) and the ANSI and ISO figures are second-hand; useful only to set the 3c and 3d check targets by what a miss costs.

Mon 16 Nov: method for every blind round (adjusted Wald interval beside each count); the ROUND3-4 intervals check at z 1.96; recheck the 4-of-5 example against Sauro and Lewis Table 1 (z 1.96 gives about 36-98%).
Mon 16 Nov: voice programme: the conceit's 2 of 24 stands, plain 20 of 24 is no gap found in 24 reads, never indistinguishable; one-sided Fisher p 0.095 checks; Keel arithmetic, so S 3.
Mon 16 Nov: method; the 19, 27 and 42 reads check by Keel arithmetic; mostly restates row 4: three-reader rounds report findings, not rates.
Mon 16 Nov: voice programme: heard as Caplet's is a similarity claim, so ISO 4120's about 60 assessors bounds what 24 reads can say; from another field.
Mon 16 Nov: voice programme: a duo-trio forced choice with Caplet's reflections as the reference replaces the surely/probably scale; a concrete change for rounds 5-6.
Mon 16 Nov: method; Nielsen's five-user formula is textbook UX; Keel's 67, 84 and 96% and the 27% for a rare misreading check.
Mon 16 Nov: method for the 3c and 3d reader panels: a clean three-reader round may be luck, so the key passages get a second round with new readers before 27 Nov.
Mon 16 Nov: method; the voice rounds already iterate; makes the rule explicit: fix, then re-test on readers who never saw the old version.
Mon 16 Nov: method: Keel's rounds give many reads but only three minds; more readers each reading fewer passages; a real fix for the voice and aha tests.
Mon 16 Nov: method for every blind read: one reader hearing owned as signed is a fix, not a vote lost 2 to 1; feeds the critical-confusion list (row 22).
Mon 16 Nov: same cognitive-interview sample-size point as row 10 (size the panel by its job); Blair and Conrad only as reported by GESIS.
Mon 16 Nov: method; test twice and fix the success rule in advance, mostly carried by row 1; applies to the aha test's words-against-chart comparison.

Mon 16 Nov: method for every reader panel: never score did-you-follow-it or a 1-5 clarity rating, only what readers say back or do; the BoE gap (0.71 self-rated, 2.02 to 2.85 of 5 tested) is the proof.
Mon 16 Nov: method: one direct and one applied question in Laura's world per check; the relatable version's 32-point gain on applied answers also backs concrete wording in 3a and 3d.
Mon 16 Nov: method for all check questions (voice, aha, exhibits): never borrow the passage's words; the BoE's own footnote is the warning.
Mon 16 Nov: method: one pilot reader answers the check questions first so a failure points at the passage; small cost on 27 Nov's schedule.
Mon 16 Nov: aha test and exhibit designs: hold reading grade fixed when words face a chart, since grade beat visuals for 4,521 adults; slides, not a paper, so S 4.
Mon 16 Nov: method for 3d's reader test: a third-party budget question (which figure does a co-sponsor's board count?), keyed to the stated bottom as SKELETON 3d says.
Mon 16 Nov: method: five-box scoring by two blind scorers with opposite readings counted apart; doubles the scoring; ANSI's wording read only in its contents note.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c and 3d: the pre-listed confusions (top owned before the move, gift outside the range, who pays it, owned heard as signed) are what the text must pre-empt as well as what tests score; Keel's list, so S 4.
Mon 16 Nov: method for the 3c range check: count a reader's figure only with the right reason (the Treasuries she owns), which stops lucky guesses at the middle.
Mon 16 Nov: explain-it-to-someone-else with expert grading is paraphrase testing (Q22-035, with Q31-033 teach-back); the co-sponsor framing can go into that row's use.
Mon 16 Nov: method for the aha tests: judgment quality (pick the plan that pays the ten whatever markets do) over recall; the rival must be a real plan, such as the team's growth-first first plan.
Mon 16 Nov: same point as row 15 (what readers say they like or understand is not evidence); the FTC's 66 readers over 8 rounds stay findable here.
Mon 16 Nov: method: faster reading is not better choosing, and an early good result needs a re-run; Beshears et al. are known in behavioural finance.
Mon 16 Nov: Book 18 (every element has a purpose) and the exhibit tests: an element readers skip or misread is a cut candidate, as the SEC cut holdings after its focus groups.
Mon 16 Nov: method; a checklist (record what was measured, before and after counts); generic, mostly covered by rows 1 and 43.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q14b-007 (test with readers like the real ones); the judge-versus-funder panel split can go into that row's use.
Mon 16 Nov: method for 3d: green and red highlighting finds the sentence that loses a funder's trust; pair it with one why question.
Mon 16 Nov: method; cloze is a cheap sentence-level check for 3c's rule sentences, cut-offs depend on the scoring rule; Taylor read only via Potter.
Mon 16 Nov: method limit: cloze misses meaning across sentences, so never use it for an aha or the whole range rule; abstracts only, so S 4.
Mon 16 Nov: method with a word payoff: blank owned in the range rule and the readers' own word (saved, set aside) tests the conceit's key term; one small charity test.
Mon 16 Nov: method for Table 2 and Figure 1: how to run the five-second look that Q23-029 holds; the 80% bar is a vendor's.
Mon 16 Nov: method: time passage tests to the minute or two a judge gives a page (BoE median 1 min 12 s), not an unhurried read.
Mon 16 Nov: method for the 3c range test: lowest, best and highest from the reader, scored against $95,000 to $115,000; both figures match NUMBERS 4.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c test: set the probe after the 2031 move; on today's figures the stated bottom itself may be $80,000-$85,000 (NUMBERS 4, 1-in-20 low), so not being surprised by $90,000 is no confusion before then.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c: readers will not guess where the gift lands, so the text must say it equals the stated top in every tested path (NUMBERS 4), within IPS l.15's choice; Dieckmann read as abstract.
Mon 16 Nov: method: a no-finance reader scored separately on 3c, 3d and 2.0's definition; here the weakest real reader is a co-sponsor's board member.
Mon 16 Nov: exhibit designs: simple tables beat funnels and histograms in the EU's PRIIPs test, backing Table 2 as a plain table and the dropped fan chart; record the McMahon 2026 tension.

Mon 16 Nov: 3.0 and 3d: fewer than half spotted the guaranteed product, so the ten owned in Treasuries must be said so plainly a skimming judge cannot miss it (guaranteed allowed, Book 19); full 2020 report not read.
Mon 16 Nov: aha test: words and chart must be equally finished, and every round keeps a control; written for persuasive ads, not a plan.
Mon 16 Nov: method; inform-not-persuade is new, anticipate-misunderstandings is already row 22 and words-and-numbers is Q4c; a hard-sell reaction counts against a passage.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a clause: Hamilton's 1813 original of store H4-028's test (only a real surplus is a sinking fund); Laura's reserve is bought with owned money, nothing borrowed.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a aha candidate: a separate account is not what makes a reserve real; owned money with nothing borrowed is, which a judge may have backwards.
Mon 16 Nov: store, 3d at most: a reserve that can be filled by borrowing says nothing by its size; Laura borrows nothing, so hers does.
Mon 16 Nov: store: Pitt's fund sized (about 26% of the funded debt, Keel arithmetic) with Hamilton's own loss estimate; adds figures to H4-027.
Mon 16 Nov: store; the use is wrong: Laura's ten pay $500,000 on far less money owned, the gap filled by Treasury interest, so it is not zero; say nothing is borrowed instead.
Mon 16 Nov: store: Parliament's own verdict corrects store H5-103 (on schedule reads too kindly); the 1829 Act's text not read, so S 4.
Mon 16 Nov: store, 3e raid example: the DMO quote stands; drop the 1733 sum until Hamilton's full page settles L.500,000 against five millions.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a or 3e: a legal wall guards a reserve's form, not its substance; corrects store H4-029; Laura has both, owned Treasuries and her two-reason rule.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; drop Pitt's flaw on day one: the 1790 borrowing clause was mainly for steadying prices, as the row's own critique says.
Mon 16 Nov: store: the first US reserve put promised payments first, the order IPS l.11 keeps.
Mon 16 Nov: store; the use is wrong: the Treasury enforces payment, not Laura keeping the bonds; her two-reason rule is her firmly-and-inviolably (card claim 4, row 41).
Mon 16 Nov: store only; serves no part, and Hamilton's 1792 purchases are admired as a rescue, a poor cautionary tale.
Mon 16 Nov: store; never call held own debt a label anywhere near the US trust funds, whose Treasuries are legal claims real to the holder (row 27).
Mon 16 Nov: store: cities moved their reserves from own paper (91% own-city in 1940) toward federal debt after the 1930s, where Laura's reserve starts.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a aha candidate (New York cancels $774m, reserve and debt vanish together); drop the use's cancel-a-Treasury-in-Laura's-reserve, which casts the doubt Book 19 rules out; say only an issuer can cancel its own bond.
Mon 16 Nov: store: New York's 1903 general fund bonds, a raid dressed as an investment.
Mon 16 Nov: store, 3e clause at most: raids came when money was tight; Laura's rule names a market fall as no reason.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a phrase candidate beside row 15 (a debt-creating instead of a debt-paying scheme); reporter citation unconfirmed, so S 4.

Mon 16 Nov: store; Table 1 lists the WInS book (bonds by CUSIP, funds by ticker), not the extra Treasuries bought in 2028; and Laura's reserve is not made by law (Q3b-033), so the court's line inverts.
Mon 16 Nov: store: officers raided reserves despite rules; Laura is owner and controller, so her rule is the guard (Q3b-033); South Houston's facts are allegations.
Mon 16 Nov: store, 3e only if fraud and custody are named (AHA_REGISTER's 5b fix): own-paper reserves escaped outside checks; Laura's holdings carry public identifiers.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.2 shape (the holder's side of a serial issue); drop no pot waiting to be raided: all ten are marketable and held until each date, so the guard is still her rule (Q3b-033).
Mon 16 Nov: store: a corporate sinking fund is a lender's covenant (textbook); Laura has no lender, so her rule does that job.
Mon 16 Nov: store: corporate practice agrees with row 13; own debt bought back is safe only when cancelled.
Mon 16 Nov: OMB's 1999 bookkeeping line alone reads as the trust funds being worthless; row 27 carries the same office's both halves; never cite it via the Heritage misquote.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a: Treasury's own books call trust-fund Treasuries an asset to the funds and a liability to Treasury that net out; always keep the asset-to-the-funds half beside it.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a's aha in official words: legal claims real to the holder, netting out only for the government as a whole; Laura is a holder; the safe wording of the card's central claim.
Mon 16 Nov: store; replace promise-to-itself with debt one part of the government owes another, netted out in consolidation; FY2024 figures, FY2025 shows $2.7tn for Social Security.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a counterweight (trust-fund Treasuries are real to holders, not worthless IOUs); fix the use: bonds pay face value on their dates, the iBond funds pay net asset value (NUMBERS 3), never a fixed sum.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a contrast from the chief actuary: redemption swaps debt owed to beneficiaries for debt owed to the public; Laura borrows nothing when hers pays.
Mon 16 Nov: store; the late-2032 coincidence is striking but invites fiscal worry; NUMBERS 8h figures (111.4% funded, $74,123 by 2042) check; a sizing contrast only.
Mon 16 Nov: store; never topped up clashes with the plan's own top-up ($2,388 in January 2028, WORDS); say nothing is added after January 2028.
Mon 16 Nov: store: the government's own funds are what it suspends at the debt limit, and made whole by statute; Laura's marketable Treasuries cannot be; Q16 rows 35-37 hold her side.
Mon 16 Nov: store, 2.3 at most: Norway's fund invests only abroad; the disanalogy (no fixed payments) is recorded.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a clause: Norway's law defines real savings as Hamilton did (nothing borrowed); new beside H3-075, H5-074 and Q7-027.
Mon 16 Nov: store; never call Norway's 2020 draw a raid or a failure: it was within its rule for a fund with no fixed liabilities; use it only as a rule with a crisis clause, which Laura's lacks.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e honest limit: a legally locked reserve in others' assets was still redirected by its owner (EUR 20.7bn), so the report names her rule as the guard, never cannot be raided.
Mon 16 Nov: store, beside row 37: a raid that loses nothing still breaks the promise; valuations are not cash.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.3: ERISA s.407's 10% cap on a sponsor's own paper anchors the reserve holding nothing tied to her career; the statute behind H7-078.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e and 3a map; fix: the raid guard is the whole two-reason rule (Walpole and New York 1903 raided for tax cuts, not market falls); drop Norway 2020 as a raid; name the fund sponsors and broker, as AHA_REGISTER's 5b fix asks.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a one-sentence aha; replace empty for the owner with OMB's cancel out for the government as a whole and keep real to the fund, so it never reads as the trust funds being worthless.
